Subject: Questions on monthly SKU smoothing and surge buffer

Hi Rishi —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. A couple of follow-ups from our side as we finalize internal procurement:

2) On the SKU-based smoothing you mentioned (converting per-token volume into a SKU for pricing tiers) — can you provide an example showing the math across a five-month launch ramp (pilot -> full launch)? We need concrete numbers for our finance team.

Appreciate it —

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on monthly SKU smoothing and surge buffer

Hi Sarah —

Thanks — that SKU sheet was helpful. High level answers first, then a short worked example attached:

- Surge buffer: we provide a monthly surge allowance tied to the committed SKU band. Unused surge in a month does NOT roll forward; however, we offer a quarterly true-up that can convert overage into a credit if you exceed committed usage in subsequent months within the same quarter.

- SKU smoothing: for pricing simplicity we map per-token usage to discrete SKUs that map to commit tiers. During a ramp we allow a step-up schedule where the committed SKU increases in specified months (you can specify months M1, M3, M5 for example). Pricing for each SKU is fixed (per-token equivalent) and discounts apply at the SKU tier level.

Attached: worked example (five-month ramp) + suggested wording for the contract SLA and true-up clause.

Next steps: Monica and I can prepare a final schedule showing month-by-month committed SKU, surge allowance, and the expected bill vs committed true-up. Suggest we lock on the month milestones first then finalize discounts.

Rishi
Director, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>

Subject: FW: Questions on monthly SKU smoothing and surge buffer

Looping finance — want to confirm margin impact and whether we can grant a 10% step discount at the M3 SKU bump. Quick asks:

- Hannah: can you run cost/margin on the proposed step-up (M1: base SKU, M3: +30%, M5: +60%) assuming 70% of tokens are chat (higher GPU time)?
- Marissa: if we offer a 10% discount at the M3 and an additional 5% at M5 (on the per-token equivalent), what does that look like to ARR and average selling price?

I prefer not to include carry-forward surge — keeps billing predictable. We can offer quarterly true-up credits as Rishi suggested.

Thanks —
Monica
Account Executive

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Aug 2027 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Questions on monthly SKU smoothing and surge buffer

Monica / team — preliminary numbers:

- Assuming the month-by-month volumes in Sarah's sheet and the channel mix (70% chat tokens), expected gross margin at list price is ~52% in months M1–M2, dips to ~47% around the M3 step (due to higher compute intensity), and recovers to ~50% by steady state (post-M5) because of amortized model warm cache gains.

- If we give a 10% discount at M3 and another 5% at M5 (stacked), margin would reduce by ~7–9 percentage points across those months; the total incremental ARR impact is modest given the short ramp window but we should preserve a minimum 40% gross margin floor.

Recommendation: approve 10% at M3 conditional on a locked-in M5 commitment (so the customer cannot step down after getting the discount). Also require a quarterly true-up clause that caps customer exposure to 120% of committed SKUs before overage rates apply.

Hannah
Finance Manager

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jensen <sarah@launch.io>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 7 Aug 2027 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on monthly SKU smoothing and surge buffer

Sarah —

Appreciate the patience while we ran the numbers. Summary and proposal:

1) Surge buffer: monthly surge allowance is non‑cumulative. We will offer a quarterly true-up that: converts overage in a quarter into credit if the customer increases committed SKU within the quarter; and caps exposure such that overage rates only kick in beyond 120% of committed SKUs for the quarter.

2) Step-up schedule (example concrete numbers):
- M1 commit: SKU-10 (equiv. 10M tokens) at $0.0009/token
- M3 commit: increase to SKU-13 (equiv. 13M tokens) — 10% discount applied to SKU-13 pricing for months M3–M5 (conditional on locked-in M5 commit)
- M5 commit: increase to SKU-16 (equiv. 16M tokens) — additional 5% discount stacked (so net ~14.5% vs list for months M5 onward)

3) Contract language: quarterly true-up clause and locked step-up commitment to prevent backdating discounts. I attached the SLA wording; if that reads OK we can generate a redline and a DocuSign.

If Launch.io is comfortable, Monica will put this schedule into the commercial exhibit and Marissa will finalize the pricing page. Hannah we appreciate the finance guardrails — please confirm the minimum margin language to include ("minimum gross margin 40% or Seller reserves right to revoke step discounts").

Would you like a short call Monday to finalize?

Thanks —
Rishi
